description:
Hey! We're Bang Ma Nuea Phom Luea Rai from Bangkok. We picked the abandoned Moon & Mars equipment challenge, and we want to dig into the data and tell the stories behind all that leftover NASA gear.
If you're into data, AI/ML, earth science, or making videos, come join us. You don't need to be a pro, just bring good vibes and ideas 😄
summary:
CERES is a free web app built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Field Shift challenge. After the rice harvest, most rain-fed fields in northeast Thailand sit empty for months. A second crop could add income and help the soil, but a failed crop wastes seed and work, and farmers cannot see how fast the soil is drying. To help rain-fed rice farmers in Thailand choose what to plant, a farmer taps their field on a map, and the app replays 25 past dry seasons for that spot, from 2001/02 to 2025/26, day by day as if the farmer had planted on that date.

Using NASA data from POWER, IMERG, SMAP, and GLDAS, plus FAO-56 crop water rules, the app compares ten crops, such as mung bean, peanut, and sesame. It shows how often each crop would have survived, the latest safe sowing date, how many waterings would make a crop safe, the estimated income per rai, and what each crop does for the soil.

The app covers all of Thailand, works in Thai and English, and runs in the browser with no server and no login. However, the team is open about its limits: the model is not calibrated, the data covers areas about 55 km wide, and some crop values are assumptions. Therefore, the app supports a farmer's choice and does not replace it.
details:
What it does

After the rice harvest most rain field in northeast Thailand sit empty for months. A second crop could add income and help the soil but a failed crop wastes seed and work and farmer can't see how fast the soil is dying. CERES lets a farmer tap their field on a map. The app takes 25 past dry seasons of NASA data for that spot and replays each one day by day as if the farmer had planted on that date. It shows how many years each of ten crops would have survived, which crop earns the most among the safe one the latest safe planting date how many watering would help and which past years look most like this season.

How it works
For every past season we run an FAO-56 soil-water model using NASA POWER rain temperature and soil witness. GPM IMERG shows this season's satellite rain, SMAP shows how wet the soil is now and GLDAS checks our model against NASA's own soil-moisture data. That check decides how confident each answer is.

Benefits and impact
Farmers get a clear answer in Thai or English on a phone with no login. They can share a link with their local extension officer, who sees the exact same result. Our goal is fewer empty fields, more income and healthier soil without guessing

Tools
React, TypeScript, Vite and MapLibre for the web app, Python for the NASA data pipeline, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages for daily data updates and hosting.

What makes it creative
Most farm tools try to predict the future. CERES replays the past instead: “this would have worked 18 of the last 25 years” is easier to trust than a forecast. It also puts income first, because that is what farmers decide on.

What we considered
Farmers use phones and read Thai so the design uses big tap choices and plain words. We are also open about the limits: the model is not yet calibrated against real fields, the data covers about 55 km per cell and pests and prices are not modelled.
